sources.title: National Disaster Preparedness Baseline Assessment: Barbados
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 national disaster-preparedness risk and vulnerability assessment with parish-level exposure, vulnerability and capacity composites.
sources.methodology: Opened the complete 124-page assessment, reviewing hazard exposure, parish vulnerability, island capacity and disaster-management findings.
sources.limitations: The maps and composite scores are multi-hazard assessments, not climate-specific causal estimates or records of observed losses.

sources.title: The Barbados Integrated Coastal Zone Management Plan, Volume 2, Segment 2
sources.organization: Coastal Zone Management Unit, Government of Barbados
sources.temporal_coverage: Volume 2 Part B and Part C of the coastal management plan dated October 2020; includes coastal risk assessment summaries and guidance for future management.
sources.methodology: Opened full 127-page Part B/C segment, including risk summaries, SWOT and national guidance.
sources.limitations: Part D sub-area maps were not reviewed; damage estimates use dated asset data and the plan is not an implementation evaluation.

sources.title: Barbados Voluntary National Review 2023
sources.organization: Government of Barbados, Office of the Prime Minister
geographic_coverage: southern and western coastal urban corridor
sources.temporal_coverage: Government SDG progress review submitted in 2023; includes 2021 Hurricane Elsa impacts and summaries of coastal-risk and resilience initiatives.
sources.methodology: Opened the full 246-page national review and read its climate, disaster-impact, coastal-risk and adaptation-program passages.
sources.limitations: The review summarizes other assessments and administrative reports; older figures and stated initiatives are not independently evaluated here.

sources.title: Barbados – Beryl Emergency Response and Recovery Project: Project Information Document
sources.temporal_coverage: Appraisal-stage project document covering Hurricane Beryl impacts in 2024, immediate recovery actions and the proposed emergency-response project.
sources.methodology: Opened the 16-page appraisal PID on Beryl impacts, sector context, response and project objectives.
sources.limitations: Appraisal PID, not completion evaluation; it cites Fisheries Division damage figures and does not attribute Beryl to climate change.

sources.title: Participatory Recovery Planning Workshop
sources.temporal_coverage: Fisherfolk survey findings and a community-recovery planning workshop held on 22 January 2026 after Hurricane Beryl.
sources.methodology: Opened the full agency post summarizing PACIFICO survey findings and the January 2026 workshop with landing-site representatives.
sources.limitations: The post does not provide the survey sample size, instrument, site-level results or sex-disaggregated findings.

sources.title: Barbados Coastal Fisheries Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: Japan-funded UNDP coastal-fisheries recovery initiative following Hurricane Beryl; the project page reports a March 2025 start, December 2027 end and ongoing status.
sources.methodology: Opened the UNDP project page and reviewed its background, objectives, expected results, dates and status.
sources.limitations: The page describes intended outputs and reports ongoing status, not evaluated outcomes; its estimate of vessel damage differs from the World Bank PID.

claims.locator: NDPBA, printed pp. 23–24, multi-hazard exposure estimates
claims.paraphrase: PDC estimates 40% of Barbados's population is exposed to flash flooding, 66% to extreme heat and 1% to coastal flooding; coastal-flood zones include 8% of critical infrastructure.
claims.limitations: Hazard-zone exposure estimates are not observed losses and are not disaggregated by parish in this table.

claims.locator: NDPBA, printed p. 37, vulnerability indicators and parish composite scores
claims.paraphrase: The composite vulnerability ranking places Saint Michael and Saint Joseph highest, followed by Saint Andrew, Saint John and Saint Lucy among Barbados's 11 parishes.
claims.limitations: The composite includes social, economic, environmental and household indicators; it is not a climate-specific ranking.

claims.locator: NDPBA, printed p. 41, island-capacity indicators and parish scores
claims.paraphrase: Island-capacity scores are highest in Saint James and lowest in Saint Joseph; Saint Andrew and Saint Lucy also rank near the bottom.
claims.limitations: The index measures selected resources and services, not observed parish-level disaster-response performance.

claims.locator: ICZM Plan, Part C §C6.1, printed pp. 166–167 (PDF pp. 79–80), coastal transportation services
claims.paraphrase: The plan reports more frequent flooding after extreme rainfall raises disruption risk along coastal links among Speightstown, Holetown, Bridgetown and Oistins, affecting tourism and freight.
claims.limitations: Flood counts and affected road segments are not supplied; the plan describes risk, not measured losses.

claims.locator: ICZM Plan, Part B2 Table B.1, printed p. 93 (PDF p. 5), coastal floodplain exposure
claims.paraphrase: The plan estimates that about 25% of the population and much infrastructure lie within a zone roughly 2 km from the coastal floodplain.
claims.limitations: This approximate plan estimate is not disaggregated by parish, household type or asset class.

claims.locator: ICZM Plan, Part B2 Table B.1, printed pp. 91–92 (PDF pp. 3–4), coastal-management SWOT findings
claims.paraphrase: The plan's 2020 SWOT identifies weak climate-adaptation and disaster-management capacity, limited coastal enforcement and weak public participation.
claims.limitations: The 2020 assessment may be dated; it does not report armed violence or link user conflicts to climate hazards.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The plan says limited stakeholder participation results in continuing conflicts among coastal sectoral user groups; it does not connect climate hazards to those conflicts.

claims.locator: VNR 2023, printed p. 158 (PDF p. 172), Hurricane Elsa recovery
claims.paraphrase: After Hurricane Elsa in 2021, the Government earmarked an initial BDS$54.5 million to repair or rebuild housing for the most vulnerable; the VNR estimates the hurricane's impact at 1% of GDP.
claims.limitations: The VNR reports an earmark, not verified expenditure or completed repairs; the event is not attributed to climate change.

claims.locator: VNR 2023, printed p. 177 (PDF p. 191), National Coastal Risk Information and Planning Platform
claims.paraphrase: The Government reports using the IDB-funded NCRIPP GIS platform and Coastal Risk Atlas to view hazard, vulnerability and risk maps for coastal and island-wide areas.
claims.limitations: The VNR describes platform use as of 2023; no map layers or operational usage records were independently reviewed.

claims.locator: VNR 2023, printed pp. 177–178 (PDF pp. 191–192), 2022 CORVI rapid assessment summary
claims.paraphrase: The VNR says CORVI found significant ecological and financial risks in the southern and western coastal urban corridor, reflecting reliance on marine and coastal activities threatened by climate change.
geographies: southern and western coastal urban corridor
claims.limitations: The VNR summarizes the 2022 CORVI assessment; detailed indicator scores and methods were not independently reviewed.

claims.locator: World Bank PID, printed pp. 2–3, paragraph 1, Hurricane Beryl damage summary
claims.paraphrase: The PID reports Beryl damaged 240 vessels, Bridgetown Port and marina breakwaters; 73% of hotels, apartments and guest houses and 40 houses also suffered damage.
claims.limitations: The vessel count is attributed to Fisheries Division; no climate attribution is made.

claims.locator: World Bank PID, printed p. 6, paragraphs 10–11, fisheries value chain and vulnerable groups
claims.paraphrase: About 3,230 fisherfolk work across roughly 30 sites; the PID says women processors and sellers faced post-Beryl pressure, selling reserves or importing fish for local demand.
claims.limitations: No site- or gender-disaggregated counts are provided; women's income losses are not quantified.

claims.locator: World Bank PID, printed pp. 3 and 6, paragraphs 2 and 11, emergency response and recovery
claims.paraphrase: The Government mobilized partners to relocate vessels, clear debris and repair Bridgetown Port; it established a Fisheries Benevolent Fund to support fisherfolk livelihoods.
claims.limitations: The PID describes early recovery; the Fund's livelihood effects are expected, not evaluated.

claims.locator: Fisheries Division post, paragraphs 1–2, survey findings and workshop held 22 January 2026
claims.paraphrase: Fisherfolk surveyed across Barbados most often reported reduced income, disrupted market and service access, and damaged or lost boats and gear; landing-site representatives met to discuss recovery priorities.
claims.limitations: The agency post does not publish sample size, methods or landing-site-specific findings.

claims.locator: UNDP Barbados Coastal Fisheries Resilience project page, Background and Expected Results
claims.paraphrase: UNDP's Japan-funded project aims to upgrade select Bridgetown Fisheries Complex infrastructure and equipment, support affected livelihoods and strengthen the fishing community's disaster preparedness through capacity building.
claims.limitations: These are project objectives, not verified results; the UNDP page estimates more than 200 damaged vessels, while the WB PID reports 240.

search_audit.query: Barbados parish-level climate vulnerability coastal flooding flash-flood and heat exposure primary reports
search_audit.outcome: Opened PDC's parish risk assessment, the government ICZM plan and VNR, plus the WB Beryl PID; named parish composites and coastal transport sites are available, but demographic data are not disaggregated within the named corridor.

search_audit.query: Barbados climate security conflict violence coastal user conflict climate-driven social tension primary evidence
search_audit.outcome: No reviewed source establishes climate change as causing violence or insecurity. The 2020 ICZM SWOT reports sectoral user conflicts linked to limited participation, but does not connect those conflicts to climate hazards; Beryl sources document livelihood impacts, not FCV violence.

search_audit.query: Barbados conflict or insecurity disrupting climate adaptation disaster response reverse FCV pathway
search_audit.outcome: No primary evidence was found that armed conflict or insecurity disrupted climate adaptation or disaster response. Reviewed sources instead describe disaster response and coastal-management constraints; no reverse-FCV claim is coded.

search_audit.query: Barbados disaster resilience capacity coastal GIS risk mapping fisheries recovery boatbuilding community preparedness government UNDP
search_audit.outcome: The VNR reports government use of NCRIPP; the WB PID documents immediate Beryl response; Fisheries Division reports fisherfolk recovery planning; UNDP describes planned fisheries infrastructure and preparedness support. Project aims are distinguished from evaluated results.

gaps: No existing BRB country baseline directory was present in the assigned worktree.

No reviewed primary source links climate stress to armed conflict, violence or insecurity in Barbados, or documents conflict/insecurity disrupting climate adaptation; this is a search gap, not evidence of absence.

The ICZM plan's reported coastal user conflicts are linked to limited stakeholder participation, not explicitly to climate hazards or violence; the plan is dated 2020 and may not represent current institutional conditions.

Parish-level PDC composites are multi-hazard and do not reveal climate-specific household or social-group vulnerability within individual coastal sites; the coastal-transport corridor evidence lacks local flood counts.
The 2026 fisherfolk survey post does not disclose sample size or site-disaggregated results; underlying survey materials were not located.
The UNDP project page and World Bank PID report different Beryl vessel-damage estimates (>200 versus 240); neither estimate was reconciled against underlying damage records.
The IDB beach-erosion profile PDF exceeded the reader size limit and the 2026 Water Authority drought article returned 403; no claims rely on indexed-only content.
